title: Oak-Braised Sweet Potato Mash with Honey Tahini
description: Sweet potatoes braise in oak-smoked broth and are mashed with a creamy honey-tahini drizzle.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with lid

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.note: Peel, remove fibrous ends and cut into 3/4-inch cubes.

ingredients.name: low-sodium mushroom broth
ingredients.note: Choose plain broth made with mushrooms and water.

ingredients.name: smooth unsalted tahini
ingredients.note: Stir the jar until the paste is homogeneous.

steps.title: Preheat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 300°F with oak pellets and the lid closed, about 15 minutes.

steps.title: Infuse the broth
steps.text: Bring {broth} to a simmer in the Dutch oven on the stove. Set the uncovered pot on the Traeger and smoke the liquid for 15 minutes with the smoker lid shut.

steps.title: Cover the potatoes
steps.text: Nestle {potatoes} into the smoked broth in a snug pot and turn to wet every piece. Fit the pot lid at the start of the braise; no stall-wrap temperature applies.

steps.title: Braise until soft
steps.text: Cook covered at 300°F for 25–40 minutes, stirring halfway. Stop when a fork passes cleanly through the thickest cubes and a cube crushes without a firm center.

steps.title: Rest in the liquid
steps.text: Rest the pot covered off heat for 5 minutes. Pour the braising liquid into a heatproof cup and reserve it.

steps.title: Make the drizzle
steps.text: Whisk {tahini}, {honey} and {lemon} in a small bowl. Beat in the warm cooking liquid a little at a time until the drizzle falls from the spoon in a thick ribbon.

steps.title: Mash and serve
steps.text: Mash the potatoes with enough of the remaining cooking liquid to make them moist and smooth. Spoon into bowls and swirl the honey tahini over both portions.

notes: Make ahead: Peel and cube the potatoes the day before, cover with water and refrigerate; drain before cooking. Refrigerate the finished mash for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the mash and tahini drizzle separately for up to 2 months. Stir both smooth after thawing. Fridge reheat: Warm a single portion, covered, in the HexClad with a splash of broth or water. Stir or turn gently and heat to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw both components overnight in the refrigerator. Reheat the mash covered to 165°F and stir the drizzle back together before serving. Option A uses a touch of lemon. For gentler Option B, leave it out and loosen the tahini with a little extra warm braising liquid. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 238 kcal, 5.1 g protein, 42.6 g total carbohydrate, 6.2 g fat, 6.2 g fiber, 113 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
